text.p: PRAVDA - The Finance Ministry said it was considering opening auctions of its treasury bills to foreign investors to help refinance the state budget deficit.
- Slovak interbank money market rates are expected to hover above 20 percent in the near future, said Martin Hrozany, chief dealer of Slovenska Sporitelna.
NARODNA OBRODA - President Michal Kovac said Slovakia still had a chance of being included in the first wave of countries which will be invited to talks on NATO enlargement this summer.

- Kovac said a referendum on integration into NATO would only make sense after official accession talks have taken place. He said that there is no reason to call such referendum this year, as planned by the governing coalition.

- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said that the OECD requires Slovakia to further liberalise its financial and banking sector in the first half of this year to complete the country's integration into the organisation by the end of 1997.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to government plans, the Slovak transport and telecommunication network should be fully compatible with European Union standards by the year 2020.
- Some 74,689 new cars were sold in Slovakia last year, compared with 24,649 cars in the previous year and 14,730 vehicles sold in 1994.
